findings.evidence: "Same shim pattern as `ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers/SKILL.md` (different target path, no shared helper yet, so it stays inline)." plus line 32 "Record the printed line as this wave's own literal value"
findings.fix: Delete the maintainer note about the sibling shim and the missing shared helper, and drop the unexplained 'wave' jargon. Keep only the command block and one line saying what to do with DETECT_FRAMEWORK_PY. This removes about 5 lines that tell the agent nothing it needs.

findings.evidence: "Either invoke it as a subprocess ... or, from Python already running with `$SKILL_DIR` on `sys.path`, `import detect_framework` as a bare top-level module"
findings.fix: Keep only the subprocess form `python3 "$DETECT_FRAMEWORK_PY" <cwd> [document_path] [signal]`. The import alternative is a menu option the agent never needs while routing.

findings.evidence: The 'live signal outranks stale document' framework sits under 'Step 0: Resolve detect_framework.py's path', separate from the Routing Procedure it governs
findings.fix: Move the paragraph 'Before routing, ask: has the user already told me which framework this is...' into Routing Procedure step 1, so the thinking frame comes right before the decision it shapes.

findings.evidence: "NEVER treat a bare filename (\"plan.md\") as \"no document_path was given.\"" says what goes wrong but gives no corrective action
findings.fix: Append: 'Resolve a bare filename to its repo-relative path first (e.g. find it under .planning/ or docs/superpowers/plans/) and pass that path; if it cannot be located, ask the user for the path.'

findings.evidence: "Routes execution of an already-generated plan/phase by detecting which framework generated it..." is declarative, and thin on casual phrasings and file keywords
findings.fix: Route execution of an already-written implementation plan or phase to the framework that generated it: a GSD phase (.planning/) goes to GSD's own /gsd-execute-phase, a superpowers plan (docs/superpowers/plans/*.md) goes to the ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers adapter. Use when the user asks to execute, run, implement, build or 'start on' a plan, phase or plan.md and which framework wrote it is not yet settled, even if they do not name GSD or superpowers. Not for writing, brainstorming or reviewing plans, or when the user already invoked /gsd-execute-phase or the superpowers adapter directly.

findings.evidence: The path shim tries only CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, ~/.claude/skills, the git toplevel and cwd, and then hard-fails
findings.fix: Add the other conformant install locations this repo targets (for example ~/.config/opencode/skills/ai-kit-spec-execute, ~/.agents/skills/ai-kit-spec-execute, ~/.codex/skills/ai-kit-spec-execute) to the for-loop. As written, a correct install under opencode or Codex hard-fails outside an ai-kit checkout.

findings.evidence: `print(detect_framework(sys.argv[1], ...))`: no --help, an IndexError traceback when no arguments are given, and plain-text output
findings.fix: Use argparse with a usage line and examples so --help works and missing cwd gives a clear error with exit code 2. Optionally add --json to emit {"framework": ..., "signal_used": ...} so the agent can confirm the signal was not dropped. Add a test for --help and for the missing-argument path in tests/test_ai_kit_spec_execute_router.py.

findings.evidence: 16 queries (8 should-trigger, 8 should-not), below the ~20 recommended
findings.fix: Add 2 should-trigger queries that never name a framework (e.g. 'ok plan looks good, start building it') and 2 near-miss negatives (e.g. 'review my superpowers plan before I run it', 'write the phase 5 plan').

findings.evidence: The exception branch packs CLI IndexError, raise conditions, permission fall-through and signal misspelling into one run-on bullet. Line 66 then says to fix the cause and not treat it as 'unknown', but line 67 asks the user the same framework question as the unknown branch
findings.fix: Split this into two branches. (a) Script error (traceback or non-zero exit): fix the invocation (missing cwd, non-string args) and re-run; do not ask the user. (b) Result does not match a non-empty CONVERSATION_SIGNAL: the signal was misspelled, so re-run with the lowercase value. Ask the user only in the 'unknown' branch.

findings.evidence: "`\"gsd\"` → hand the plan to GSD's own `/gsd-execute-phase <phase>`" does not say how to get <phase> when the user gave only a file path or nothing
findings.fix: Add: 'Take <phase> from the user's request or from the NN- prefix of the .planning/phases/ directory holding the document; if neither gives it, ask for the phase number before invoking.'
